STEP 1 - Scene: This is a buffet-style sampler plate with a whole Asian pear, a single pork rib strip, a roasted chicken thigh/drumstick piece, and one piece of California roll sushi.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The vessel is a round white dinner plate, about 27 cm across with a wide rim. Its area is 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Asian pear (whole)
- Barbecued pork rib (single strip)
- Roasted chicken leg piece
- California roll piece

STEP 4 - Area: Food covers about 30% of the plate in total.

| Item | Share of plate | Area |
|---|---|---|
| Pear | 11% | 63 cm² |
| Rib | 9% | 51 cm² |
| Chicken | 9% | 51 cm² |
| Sushi | 1.5% | 9 cm² |

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Pear: about 8.5 cm in diameter, so treated as a sphere: about 320 ml.
- Rib: 51 cm² × 2.5 cm height = 128 ml.
- Chicken: 51 cm² × 3 cm height = 153 ml.
- Sushi: 9 cm² × 2.5 cm height = 22 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Pear: the volume is a solid sphere, so I use a density of 0.85, giving about 270 g.
- Rib: the bone is included, so I use an edible density of about 0.75, giving about 95 g.
- Chicken: with bone, I use 0.75, giving about 115 g.
- Sushi: 22 ml × 1.0 = about 22 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:

| Item | Grams | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pear | 270 | 42 | 113 |
| Rib (edible portion, plus bone averaged in) | 95 | 260 | 247 |
| Chicken with skin | 115 | 200 | 230 |
| Sushi | 22 | 150 | 33 |

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The total is about 500 g and about 623 kcal. That is plausible for a large whole pear plus three small protein and starch portions.
